title: Pre-Microporation Improves Outcome of Pancreatic Islet Labelling for Imaging
author: Herynek, Gálisová, et al.
materials: We used pancreatic islets from Brown-Norway and Lewis rats. Pancreatic islets were isolated according to a protocol described by Gotoh [36]. Briefly, collagenase (1 mg/ml; Sevapharma, Prague, Czech Republic) was injected intraductally, after which the distended pancreas was excised and gently shaken at 37 °C for 20 min. Islets were separated from exocrine tissue using centrifugation in a discontinuous Ficoll® gradient (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA). Isolated islets were cultured for 24 h (37 °C, 5% CO2 atmosphere) in a CMRL-1066 medium (PANBiotech GmbH, Aidenbach, Bavaria, Germany) supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum (FBS), 5% HEPES and 1% penicillin/streptomycin/L-glutamine (all Sigma-Aldrich).

The electroporation device Neon Transfection System (ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) was used for the experiment. Buffers from the original Neon™ Transfection System 100 μL Kit (ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) were used. The Neon Tube was filled by 3 mL of electrolytic Buffer E2 and the tube was placed into the Neon Pipette Station. One hundred and ten microliters samples containing 250 pancreatic islets resuspended in the Buffer R with suspended nanoparticles (the final nanoparticle concentration was the same at 23 mg/mL medium) were prepared. The islets were aspired into a 100 μL pipette tip and placed in the Neon Tube with the Electrolytic Buffer E2 according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The islets were then microporated using one, two, or four 20 ms pulses. The pulse voltage varied in the range 600–1500 V (electric field 20–50 kV/m). After microporation, the pipette was immediately removed and the microporated islets were placed in wells and kept on ice for 10 min. The islets were then collected and placed in Petri dishes containing 3 mL of medium without antibiotics and incubated at 37 °C for 24 h. After incubation, pancreatic islets were collected, washed three times using PBS, hand-picked and counted under a microscope.

steps.title: Isolate pancreatic islets
steps.instruction: Inject collagenase (1 mg · mL⁻¹; Sevapharma) intraductally into the pancreas of Brown‑Norway or Lewis rats, excise the distended pancreas, and gently shake at 37 °C for 20 min; separate islets from exocrine tissue by centrifugation in a discontinuous Ficoll® gradient (Sigma‑Aldrich).

steps.title: Culture isolated islets
steps.instruction: Culture the isolated islets for 24 h at 37 °C in a 5 % CO₂ atmosphere in CMRL‑1066 medium (PANBiotech) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum, 5 % HEPES, and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin/L‑glutamine (all Sigma‑Aldrich).

steps.title: Prepare Neon electroporation system (standard)
steps.instruction: Insert a Neon Tube into the Neon Pipette Station and fill the tube with 3 mL electrolytic Buffer E2 (Neon™ 100 µL Kit, ThermoFisher).

steps.title: Standard microporation of islets
steps.instruction: Resuspend 250 pancreatic islets in 110 µL Buffer R containing suspended nanoparticles (final nanoparticle concentration = 23 mg · mL⁻¹ medium). Aspirate the suspension into a 100 µL pipette tip and place the tip into the Neon Tube containing Buffer E2. Microporate using one, two, or four pulses of 20 ms each; set pulse voltage between 600 V and 1500 V (electric field 20–50 kV · m⁻¹). Immediately remove the tip, transfer the microporated islets to a well and keep on ice for 10 min. Then collect the islets, place them in a Petri dish with 3 mL medium lacking antibiotics, and incubate at 37 °C for 24 h. After incubation, wash the islets three times with PBS, hand‑pick, and count under a microscope.

steps.title: Prepare Neon electroporation system (pre‑microporation)
steps.instruction: Insert a Neon Tube into the Neon Pipette Station and fill the tube with 3 mL electrolytic Buffer E2 (Neon™ 100 µL Kit, ThermoFisher).

steps.title: Pre‑microporation without nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Prepare 96‑well plate wells with 110 µL medium containing suspended nanoparticles at 46 mg · mL⁻¹. Prepare a 110 µL sample containing 250 pancreatic islets in pure Buffer R (no nanoparticles). Aspirate the islet suspension into a 100 µL pipette tip and place the tip into the Neon Tube with Buffer E2. Microporate using two pulses of 20 ms each at 500–1000 V (electric field 16.5–33 kV · m⁻¹). Immediately transfer the microporated islets into the wells containing 110 µL nanoparticle‑laden medium; the final nanoparticle concentration after mixing becomes 23 mg · mL⁻¹. Keep the islets on ice for 10 min, then collect them and place in a Petri dish with 3 mL medium without antibiotics. Incubate at 37 °C for 24 h. After incubation, wash three times with PBS, hand‑pick, and count under a microscope.

steps.title: Optimised pre‑microporation workflow
steps.instruction: Perform pre‑microporation of islets (no nanoparticles) using two 20 ms pulses at 600 V (electric field ≈ 20 kV · m⁻¹). Immediately place the microporated islets into medium containing suspended nanoparticles so that the final nanoparticle concentration is 23 mg · mL⁻¹. Keep the suspension on ice for 10 min, then transfer the islets to a Petri dish with 3 mL antibiotic‑free medium and incubate at 37 °C for 24 h (incubation may be shortened if necessary). Finally, wash three times with PBS, hand‑pick, and count.
